title: Integer Products: Building the Sign Rule
preview: A 9-step thin-slice that walks groups from 4 × 3 to (-4) × (-3), one tiny variation at a time, so the sign rule emerges instead of being told.

body.goal: Students notice and articulate the sign rule for multiplying integers by walking through carefully chosen variations rather than being told a procedure.
body.launch: Tell the class: 'I'm going to give you a sequence of problems, one at a time. After each one, talk in your group about what changed and what stayed the same.' Random groups, vertical whiteboards. Don't lecture about negatives first.

steps.teacherNote: Pause here. 'What pattern do you see?' Listen for: 'It's going down by 4.'
First negative result. Don't help — let the pattern argue for them.
Consolidate: 'positive × negative = ?' Get a class statement on the board.
Switch the sign. 'Why does this still come out -12?' Commutative property emerges.
The big one. Resist explaining — let groups argue. Use the (-4) × {3, 2, 1, 0, -1, -2, -3} pattern table to anchor it.

body.consolidation: Bring the class back. Ask: 'In one sentence, when do you get a positive answer? When do you get a negative answer?' Write the rule on the board ONLY after a student says it.
